name: Envision Energy (Envision Group / AESC)
headquarters: Shanghai, China (founded in Jiangyin, Jiangsu; US offices: Burlington MA, California; AESC US plants in TN/KY/SC)
ownership: private (Envision Group; no cap table published. Battery arm AESC's reported investors include Nissan, GIC, Keppel, HongShan, and Primavera; AESC explored a $1-2B Hong Kong IPO per Bloomberg, Apr 2026)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Envision is the capability-tier-1, volume-tier-2 giant of the field — Wood Mackenzie's 2026 global BESS integrator ranking puts it tied 5th with Trina (behind Sungrow, Tesla, CATL, BYD) on comprehensiveness, while InfoLink's 2025 volume top tier omits it entirely. It is the world's #2 wind OEM (BNEF 2025, 20.9 GW), owns its cells through AESC (790 Ah LFP in mass production from Apr 2026; >50 GWh BESS delivered across 400+ projects, company-claimed), and runs the strongest AI-data-center storyline of any Chinese storage player: Mission Gobi (5 GW of green AIDC by 2030), the GW-scale Galaxy Campus in Ulanqab, and the all-renewable Chifeng AIDC. But its US position is upstream, not systems: named in NDAA §154 (DoD battery ban from Oct 2027) alongside Hithium, it restructured by selling control of AESC's Smyrna TN cell plant to US-controlled Fixx Energy (Apr 2026) — whose cells now supply ~50% of Fluence's US project cells and a 10 GWh Prevalon deal. Envision arms the FEOC-compliant competition rather than competing in the US itself.
ecosystemRole: We assess Envision as the closest strategic comparable to Hithium in the entire Batch A set — the other NDAA §154-named Chinese storage major — and as the author of the playbook Hithium would have to study for US access: the Fixx restructuring (sell control of the US plant to a US entity, retain a minority stake plus technology licensing, let the cells flow to US integrators as domestic content) is the only executed template for converting a statutorily-named Chinese battery maker's US assets into FEOC-tolerable supply. Whether that structure survives Treasury's final FEOC regulations is the single biggest open question in the US market's China policy stack. Outside the US, Envision is a direct heavyweight competitor in every geography Hithium targets — Europe (1.6 GWh Germany single project), South Africa, Central Asia, India — usually bundling wind, storage, localization, and vendor financing.

productsAndServices.name: Gen 8 Scalable Platform (flagship LDES BESS)
productsAndServices.description: Full rollout announced at Tech Day Beijing, Oct 27, 2025: 10-foot modular skid units on the 750+ Ah AESC cell; configurations 6/8/10/12 MWh (and larger) per unit; each unit <29 tons (road-transport friendly); supports >4-hour durations; installation/commissioning time cut up to 30%; 26% smaller footprint for typical 4-h systems; 12% lower auxiliary consumption; ~1% IRR uplift claimed for a 100 MW/4-h project vs a 5 MWh baseline. Sold with the GEN 8 AC TwinSkid MV System (10 MVA AC skid = four parallel 2.5 MW PCS) and EnOS-based SCADA/EMS/Hybrid Power Plant Controller. First deliveries: Germany with ju:niz Energy, 140.6 MWh grid-forming (Jul 2026).
productsAndServices.positioning: Modular-skid alternative to the 20-ft container orthodoxy — the 'and larger than 12 MWh' roadmap plus a separately trade-press-reported 12.5 MWh AI-native container (ESIE, Apr 2026: SiC PCS at 99.3% efficiency, grid-forming, minute-level black start) put Envision at the density frontier.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Integrated BESS supply, full turnkey EPC (Kallista Saleux: EPC + ≥14-yr LTSA), supply agreements with LTSAs (Field: 15-yr), localization JVs (Kazakhstan Samruk-Kazyna; SUN Terra Indonesia incl. technology licensing), and a $500M BBVA vendor-financing wrap.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility-scale standalone and renewables-paired storage; wind+storage hybrids via the proprietary HPPC; AI/data-center power ('Powering AI Infrastructure' is one of the storage page's three core scenarios).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Gen 8 configurations beyond 12 MWh; Mission Gobi AIDC build-out; sodium-ion option entering the mix (AESC >180 Ah Na-ion cell in production Mar 2026, pitched at AIDC backup).

productsAndServices.name: Gen 7 / EN 5 Pro + EN ACSkid-10000 (grid-forming stack)
productsAndServices.description: Gen 7: 5 MWh DC container + 5 MWh string PCS + TwinSkid MV (5500/6900 kVA) — deployed at e.g. Pulse Clean Energy UK (310 MWh, 2.4-h optimized). EN 5 Pro (Smarter E 2025): 2.5 MW/5 MWh all-in-one string-PCS container — DC+AC in one, pre-lithiated cells with zero degradation for the first 3 years, >99% PCS efficiency claim via SiC, grid-forming at SCR ≥1.0, seamless on/off-grid transitions, black start. EN ACSkid-10000 (Smarter E 2025): 5.05 MW grid-forming PCS, 4-20 s synthetic inertia, withstands 1.5× rated short-circuit current for 10 s.
productsAndServices.positioning: 'Market Leader, Advancing Grid Forming Solution For Next-Gen Power System' — grid-forming is the through-line of the whole portfolio, from PCS to the AI Power System framing.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Same channels as Gen 8; vertically integrated 'from R&D through MV connection' including delivery, installation, and long-term O&M.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Frequency regulation, capacity markets, black start, weak-grid interconnections.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Gen 7 running alongside Gen 8 during transition; SST (solid-state transformer) + 800 V DC AIDC variants shown at The smarter E 2026.

productsAndServices.name: AESC cells (the vertical-integration layer — and the US story)
productsAndServices.description: Envision's battery arm (acquired 2019; founded in Japan 2007 as Nissan's cell JV): 300+/500+/700+ Ah ESS cell ladder; 790 Ah LFP mass production from Apr 2026 at Cangzhou (claimed world's largest prismatic wound storage cell: >440 Wh/L, 15,000+ cycles, 30-yr calendar life, 96% RTE); >180 Ah sodium-ion in production Mar 2026 (−40 to 70 °C, 20,000 cycles). InfoLink: 4th in 2024 non-China-market storage cell shipments; >30 GWh of 300+ Ah cells delivered; supplies third-party integrators Fluence, Powin (now Flexgen assets), Nidec. 13 manufacturing sites across Japan, US, UK, France, Spain, China.
productsAndServices.positioning: The US access vehicle: Smyrna TN (ex-Nissan LEAF plant, retooled 2025 to ~3 GWh/yr LFP storage cells) was sold to US-controlled Fixx Energy (control from Apr 1, 2026; AESC retains minority + licensing) — its cells supply ~50% of Fluence's US project LFP and a 3-year 10 GWh Prevalon deal. Bowling Green KY ($2.0B, 30 GWh, Mercedes-linked) continues; Florence SC ($1.6B, 30 GWh, BMW-linked) had construction halted Jun 2025 with the base plant still targeting 2026 production.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Merchant cell supply to US/global integrators; internal supply to Envision systems (all named EU/UK projects specify AESC LFP — Douai France 10 GWh plant supplies European projects).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: US domestic-content BESS (via Fixx), EV OEMs (Nissan, Mercedes, BMW), Envision's own systems.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Reported $1-2B AESC Hong Kong IPO (Bloomberg, Apr 2026); open legal question whether Envision's continuing license/IP role taints the FEOC status of Smyrna cells under Treasury's final regs (due late 2026).

productsAndServices.name: AI Power System / AIDC initiatives (Mission Gobi, Galaxy Campus, Chifeng)
productsAndServices.description: Mission Gobi (launched VivaTech, Jun 18, 2026): 5 GW of green AI-data-center capacity in desert/arid regions by 2030 — claims 1% of global desert could host terawatt-scale computing. Galaxy Campus, Ulanqab: billed as the world's only GW-scale AIDC powered by directly connected renewables (first building commissioned ~Aug 6, 2026; designed to scale beyond 2 GW, up to 1M AI accelerators). Chifeng Net Zero Industrial Park: 'world's first AIDC powered entirely by renewable electricity' — 2 GW renewable system, grid-forming storage, 1.5M t/yr green ammonia, Tencent computing-task scheduling. Product layer: 'AI Power System' — SST + 800 V DC battery (LFP or Na-ion), EnOS energy-IoT OS, Dubhe energy foundation model, AI trading loop (claimed +4-8% project IRR).
productsAndServices.positioning: The strongest AIDC narrative of any Chinese storage vendor — but demonstrated in China's deserts, not the US; no US data-center storage deal exists.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Own-development showcases (Chifeng, Ulanqab) plus replication partnerships under the Mission Gobi banner.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: AI/cloud operators seeking off-grid or direct-renewable campuses; governments courting AIDC investment.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 5 GW by 2030 target; positioning as blueprint exporter ('AI power systems' as the product).

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Envision as capability-tier-1 but volume-tier-2: Wood Mackenzie scores it tied 5th globally on its 10-criteria methodology while InfoLink's 2025 shipment top tier (Tesla, Sungrow, BYD, Huawei, CRRC) omits it — meaning Envision wins on vertical integration, grid-forming depth, and bankability attributes, not on raw GWh, and its rank slipped 4th → tied 5th as CATL/BYD surged.

(High confidence) We assess Envision's US strategy as 'arm the compliant competition': named in NDAA §154 (DoD ban from Oct 2027) and FEOC-walled from direct ITC-linked sales, it converted its US cell asset into influence — the Fixx-controlled Smyrna plant supplies ~50% of Fluence's US LFP and 10 GWh to Prevalon as domestic content, while Envision keeps a minority stake and licensing income. No Envision-branded system sells into the US.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the Fixx structure's survival under Treasury's final FEOC regulations (due late 2026) as the single biggest open question in this file: if continuing licensing/IP ties are ruled to taint effective-control status, the Smyrna cells lose their domestic-content halo and both Fluence's and Prevalon's supply narratives take damage — a systemic event for the US mid-tier, not just for Envision.

(High confidence) We assess the AIDC storyline as the strongest of any Chinese storage vendor — Mission Gobi, the GW-scale Galaxy Campus, all-renewable Chifeng, SST + 800 V DC products, and the EnOS/Dubhe software stack — but note it is entirely China-proven: zero US data-center storage deals, and its US AIDC exposure is indirect (cells into Fluence's pipeline).

(High confidence) For the Hithium lens: Envision is the closest strategic comparable — the other NDAA §154-named storage major — and its playbook defines Hithium's realistic US option space: (a) upstream domestic-content supply through a US-controlled manufacturing entity (the Fixx template), (b) capability-led differentiation (grid-forming, fire-test proof points, vendor financing) in Europe/MEA/Asia where both can still bid, and (c) an energy-first AIDC pitch. Everywhere outside the US, expect to meet Envision in the final round — usually bundling wind, localization, and financing that a pure-play battery maker cannot match.
